name: TickTagGO Task Manager
author: skymiis

sections.description:
Manage personal tasks and to-do lists inside your WordPress dashboard. TickTagGO brings its lavender workspace to each signed-in user’s existing WordPress account. No additional TickTagGO account, payment, API key or companion plugin is needed.

The interface is rendered directly in the WordPress admin page using PHP and bundled JavaScript and styles. It does not embed an internal or remote page in an iframe.

  • Create and switch between boards using tabs. Rename boards and delete empty boards.
  • Organize tasks in two to six configurable stages; drag cards, use a touch grip or use Alt and arrow keys to move them.
  • Use a board, a task list, an archive or a monthly calendar.
  • Quickly add tasks, or edit titles, descriptions, due dates and priorities in the detailed editor.
  • Format notes with bold, italic and text color. Add checklists, completion marks, labels and dated comments.
  • Search task text across boards, including notes, descriptions, checklists and comments. Filter by labels and deadlines.
  • Duplicate, archive, restore and permanently delete tasks with confirmation. Undo and redo edits in the current session; permanent deletion clears that task from undo history.
  • Retain view, search, calendar month, scroll and display-size preferences.
  • Optionally keep the workspace on top in browsers that support Document Picture-in-Picture. The standard dashboard remains available in other browsers.
  • Save password-encrypted .ticktaggo backups in the new TWBK v1 format. Import new backups or legacy .donext DNX1 files. Choose to add boards or replace the workspace.
  • Use bundled interfaces in 13 languages, including Arabic right-to-left layout. The WordPress user’s language selects the interface.

All included features are free. There is no genre-count quota, payment, license check or upgrade required to add boards.

Each signed-in user manages their own workspace, including subscribers. This is personal task management; team boards, assignments and live collaboration are not provided. HTTPS (or localhost for local testing) is required for browser cryptography and task identifiers.

Privacy and storage

Tasks and view preferences are saved in this site’s WordPress database, associated with the current user’s ID. Reading and saving tasks sends data to this site. The plugin does not encrypt this database data. Site administrators, database operators and backup owners may have access. There is no developer telemetry or transmission of task data to the developer.

Password-protected .ticktaggo files use a versioned TWBK v1 container with an authenticated header. Files are encrypted in the browser with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and AES-256-GCM. File passwords are not sent to the server or stored permanently. Losing the password means the encrypted file cannot be recovered by this plugin. Importing a decrypted file saves its tasks to the site’s database. New backups cannot be opened in older DoNext apps.

Google Drive is an optional manual file destination: export a .ticktaggo file, upload it yourself, then download/import it elsewhere. TickTagGO does not connect to the Drive API or provide automatic synchronization. Files uploaded by you are handled by that service.

Deactivation and plugin removal preserve task data. “Delete all my task data” clears your live task payload and preferences; a user ID, version token and timestamp remain to reject stale saves. WordPress personal-data erasure removes the entire plugin record for that user. WordPress user deletion also removes their live workspace. Existing server backups and exported files are managed separately.

A save is limited to 2 MiB and 5,000 tasks total; the supported schema accepts 500 labels. These resource bounds do not have a paid unlock. Unknown future fields and floating-panel coordinates are not retained. DNX2 device recovery files cannot be imported; export DNX1 with a password in the original DoNext app first.
sections.installation:
1. Open Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin in WordPress.
  2. Select ticktaggo-task-manager-1.2.1.zip, install it and activate TickTagGO Task Manager.
  3. Sign in with your own WordPress account and open TickTagGO in the admin menu.
  4. Select a board tab, add a task and wait for “Saved to WordPress”.
  5. Use Settings to export encrypted copies or import a .ticktaggo or legacy .donext file. Export your existing tasks before replacing the workspace.

When moving from DoNext Task Manager 1.1.2 on the same site, export a backup, deactivate DoNext, then install and activate TickTagGO. Existing per-user workspaces are retained in the same database table. No task data is copied to another owner. Do not use both interfaces at the same time. To return to the previous plugin, deactivate TickTagGO and reactivate the preserved DoNext plugin; the server workspace remains available.

This release is intended for individual WordPress sites. Network-wide activation and multisite-wide privacy processing have not been validated.
sections.faq:
Can subscribers use it?

Yes. A WordPress account with the read capability can open TickTagGO and manage its own tasks. Site administrators control account creation and site access.

Are tasks private from site administrators?

Users are separated in the plugin UI and API. The site’s database is not encrypted by this plugin, so administrators and database/backup operators may have access.

Can I use several devices?

Sign in to the same WordPress account on this site to load saved tasks. Changes are not pushed live to already-open tabs. A stale save is rejected; export a copy and reload if a conflict appears.

What happens if saving fails?

Keep the page open, export an encrypted copy if needed and retry from Settings. For an expired session or a conflict, export a copy before signing in again or reloading. Unsaved edits live only in the open page.

Can I transfer data from DoNext Web or Chrome?

Yes, using password-protected DNX1 files. Import adds boards within the workspace resource bounds, or replaces the current workspace after confirmation. Notes, labels, comments, priorities and checklists in the known version-1 format are retained and editable.

What format does TickTagGO export?

TickTagGO exports .ticktaggo files in the TWBK v1 authenticated container format. Older .donext DNX1 files can be imported for migration. New backups require an application that supports TWBK v1; renaming the extension does not make them compatible with older apps.

What happens when I uninstall?

Task data is retained. Delete your workspace or use WordPress privacy erasure before removing the plugin if you want to remove live data. Backups and downloaded files need separate deletion.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Add a standard WordPress admin page heading and a correctly sized menu logo.
  • Keep the interface directly in the WordPress admin document without internal or remote iframes.
  • Retain existing tasks, translations, backup formats and all included free features.

1.2.0

  • Adopt the TickTagGO name, new original logo and ticktaggo-task-manager text domain.
  • Preserve existing DoNext WordPress workspaces and all included free features.
  • Export authenticated TWBK v1 .ticktaggo backups and import legacy DNX1 files.
  • Update 13 language interfaces and resource-limit guidance.

1.1.2

  • Fix blank dashboard compatibility with script-tag rewriting using a self-contained local browser script.
  • Read startup settings from escaped HTML and display loading or connection failures.
  • Bound REST waits and retain existing tasks on failed startup.

1.1.1

  • Remove the genre-count quota from board creation, saving and file import.
  • Remove upgrade guidance and update all 13 language interfaces.
  • Check workspace capacity before committing a new board.
  • Preserve existing task data and encrypted backup compatibility.

1.1.0

  • Add board creation, tabs and board settings.
  • Bring the full DoNext workspace UI, list, calendar, configurable stages and detailed task editor.
  • Add rich notes, priorities, labels, checklists, comments, duplicate and search across boards.
  • Replace raw task-metadata display with direct editing controls.
  • Add safe import merging, permanent-delete history clearing, bounded edit validation and retryable saves.
  • Add language-specific UI templates and WordPress.org translation extraction.
  • Preserve 1.0.0 workspaces, DNX1 compatibility and per-user WordPress storage.

1.0.0

  • Initial independent distribution: per-user storage, compact UI, DNX1 backups and 13-language interface.
